column7: 2026-11-05: Billing display rule from finance: never show more than actually used, so bytes.format must truncate extra decimals, never round up (1048575 B -> 1023.99KB, not 1MB or 1024KB; 2047 B -> 1.99KB). Reason: support saw '1024KB' on billing page, caused by toFixed rounding up near unit boundaries (index.js format). Status: code NOT changed yet; waiting on finance to sign off the page wording.

2026-11-05: Capacity-alerts rule from ops: never show less than real usage, so bytes.format rounds UP (ceil) at the shown precision (1048575 B -> 1MB, 1025 B -> 1.01KB, 2047 B -> 2KB). Opposite of billing-ui (truncate). Reason: alerts must not understate usage. Status: only described, code NOT changed; ops still reviewing alert thresholds. Suggested: a shared rounding option (up/down/nearest) rather than hardcoding either rule.

2026-11-05: format() now truncates via Math.trunc(val*10^dp)/10^dp instead of toFixed rounding; code changed, tests added/updated (old tests expecting round-half-up, e.g. 1.5KB dp0 -> 2KB, now expect truncation). Finance wording sign-off still pending on the page itself.
